content:
Seeed Studio sent us two e-paper kits preloaded with OpenDisplay open-source firmware for review: the OpenDisplay 4.26″ Mono Kit and OpenDisplay 7.3″ Color Kit, both powered by a Nordic nRF52840 low-power Bluetooth LE microcontroller. This review focuses on practical use of the preinstalled OpenDisplay firmware: sending images from a browser, configuring the devices with OpenDisplay Toolbox, and connecting them to Home Assistant to create dashboards that update automatically with data from around the home. Unboxing Seeed Studio OpenDisplay e-paper kits and hardware overview Both models arrive fully assembled, with a display, a driver board, a XIAO nRF52840 Plus board, a battery, and a white 3D-printed enclosure. The only difference between the two kits is the display; the MCU, 2,000 mAh battery, and number of buttons are the same. Both models have a power switch, a reset button, three push buttons, a USB-C port, and one mounting hole. The 3D enclosure [...]
